params.description: Progressive opening: a hidden boolean cutter keyed at fractions t of the action interval (location/rotation/scale); bind the interval to camera cues 'cam-<mark>' so it finishes before the camera arrives

also_cut_overlapping.description: also cut every static, closed, render-visible mesh overlapping the cutter's final volume (road markings, kerbs); animated objects are skipped and listed

params.description: Baked at build (studio/blender_ops/simulate.py): rigid_debris falls onto the action targets (passive colliders); dust drifts. Starts at start_frame; bind to camera/speech cues with time_binding.

ceiling_z.description: dust only: the top of the drift (default: the region top)

target_anchor.description: what a keyed camera is about: keys without target aim at it, and the build fails if it leaves the frame (keyed cameras only)

target.description: where the camera looks; omit it to aim at camera.target_anchor at that frame

no_pass_through.description: fail when the camera's frame-to-frame step crosses a render-visible mesh (evaluated per frame, so reveals count)

clip_auto.description: set clip_start below half the closest clearance (<= 0.1 m) and clip_end past the farthest geometry; fails if the camera comes closer than clip_start

graphic_in_frame.description: fail when a render-visible graphic (title, 3D text) is cut by the frame edge for more than 2 frames (default true)

framing_tolerance.description: largest horizon error allowed while framing holds (default 0.02 of the frame height)

timing.description: Progress along the move u(t): burst_settle rushes to burst_share by burst_frac of the shot, decelerates, creeps drift over the last hold_frac

scope.description: all: offset/aim/lens keys follow the same progress

head_frac.description: slow head before the burst (creeps head_share of the move)

sweep_deg.description: orbit with timing: total angle swept over the shot

framing.description: compiled framing: horizon held at horizon_v until release_frame, then smoothstep over blend_frames to the aim

guard_target.description: What the look-target guard watches when the camera aims elsewhere (a move aiming through a helper sets it to its target); default: look_target

target_blur_px.description: scene motion-blur target (px at p95 screen speed); labels keep their own 2 px cap

move.description: Semantic camera move compiled into a flythrough/orbit rig at build (camera_moves.py): what to show, the numbers come from the style and camera fit

timing.description: Progress along the move u(t): burst_settle rushes to burst_share by burst_frac of the shot, decelerates, creeps drift over the last hold_frac

scope.description: all: offset/aim/lens keys follow the same progress

head_frac.description: slow head before the burst (creeps head_share of the move)

whip_in_deg.description: yaw added over the first 0.25 s (whip transition into the shot)

no_pass_through.description: fail when the camera's frame-to-frame step crosses a render-visible mesh (evaluated per frame, so reveals count)

clip_auto.description: set clip_start below half the closest clearance (<= 0.1 m) and clip_end past the farthest geometry; fails if the camera comes closer than clip_start

graphic_in_frame.description: fail when a render-visible graphic (title, 3D text) is cut by the frame edge for more than 2 frames (default true)

framing_tolerance.description: largest horizon error allowed while framing holds (default 0.02 of the frame height)

arrive.description: Meaning before rhythm: the camera may not pass a mark before a time (e.g. the road must finish opening). camera fit treats it as a hard penalty and slows the head.

framing.description: Hold the horizon at screen height horizon_v (0 = top) until a camera cue, then blend to the move's own aim: an establishing frame reads open (sky above the street) before the move looks down into its target

hold_until_cue.description: camera cue that ends the hold (absent: hold the whole shot)

dwell.description: linger at camera cues: the progress curve nearly stops around the cue for `seconds` (eased in and out), every later cue moves accordingly - 'stop in front of the section and let it read'

motion_style.description: library/motion_styles/<name>.json the shot's measured motion is checked against

sentence_claims.description: One entry per narration sentence (studio/facts.py): the claims it rests on, or why it is not a claim

atmosphere.description: Opt-in fog volume + light beams built by the look's lighting pass (photoreal presets). Explanatory atmosphere (structure lit by shafts) stays in Blender; real-place haze/smoke routes to generation (routing R5).

look_style.description: overrides style.look.look_style for this shot (a night aerial in a day reel)

composition_style.description: composition style (library/composition_styles) the shot's framing is checked against (advisory)

composition_span_s.description: seconds of the shot the composition check covers (e.g. the establishing head)

exposure_keys.description: frames metered on their own (night street -> lit interior); deltas keyed on a compositor Exposure node, eased over transition_frames centred on the key

grade.description: Colour grade after the look (blender_ops/expressive.py): exposure_offset_ev adds to the metered exposure, exposure replaces it

compositor.description: Compositor ops spliced in before the look output, in order (expressive_core.COMPOSITOR_OPS)

engine_settings.description: Render engine settings by RNA name (expressive_core.ENGINE_SETTINGS); what the renderer sets itself is refused

addons.description: Add-ons bundled with Blender, enabled for the build (not for render workers)

graphics.description: Explainer graphics drawn as Grease Pencil into their own transparent layer (graphics render), composited by the edit under labels; never in the beauty render, control passes or generative inputs.

text.description: dimension only: 'auto' writes the measured length ('12.9 m'); any other string is drawn as given

space.description: world (default): anchored in the scene. screen: drawn in the frame (arrows), constant size, checked for legibility

points_2d.description: screen arrows: tail and tip in normalized frame coordinates (0,0 top-left)

shaft_frac.description: screen arrows: stroke width as a share of the frame height (default 0.0075)

head_ratio.description: screen arrows: head length / stroke width (default 3.5; legible 3-4.5)

fade_frames.description: screen arrows: linear fade in and out (default 8)

titles.description: 2D titles composited in the edit (studio/titles.py): anchored to the frame, checked against the title safe rectangle every frame. Use instead of 3D text for anything that must stay readable.

anchor.description: frame position of the ink's alpha centroid (x, y from top-left)

width_frac.description: ink width at scale 1 as a fraction of the frame width

weight.description: face style name in the pinned font collection (ExtraBold, Heavy, ...)

scale_curve.description: recede: scale at evenly spaced times over the title's span (monotone cubic between)

fill_brief.description: What fills the shot's levels, decided by topic with the user (studio/fill.py): proposed by the agent, revised and approved in the user's words. Renders and paid generation need it approved.

void.description: left empty on purpose (exempt from FILL_LEVEL_EMPTY); say why in note

role.description: subject: what the shot explains; identity: the fewest cues that say where we are; ambient: life

element.description: library exemplar id (a trailing * picks every matching exemplar, e.g. pedestrian_*) or subject:<subject_id> for a project spec

edge.description: along_edge: which long edge of the level area (near = toward the section face)

at.description: line_across / cluster: position along the area's long axis from the section face (0) to the far end (1)

why.description: traced to the request, narration, a reference or the user's words

height_m.description: mount height above the level floor (ceiling pipes, hanging signs); default 0 = standing on the floor

parents.description: approved decision layers this brief was approved against (studio/decisions.py)

key_parts.description: Parts the frame probe must see (studio/blender_ops/frame_probe.py): an explain shot fails when one never shows in its window; ids are studio ids or part paths (inst/part)

min_px.description: pixels at the probe height (256 px) below which the part does not count as seen

start_s.description: reference applies from this time (s) - written into the prompt

previs.description: How the Blender motion pass encodes intent for the video model (hybrid)

orientation_colors.description: clay pass tints each subject's forward faces red and rear faces blue (spec length axis = forward); the prompt says so

part_ids.description: subject_id/part_id or studio_id of objects shown black; omit = nothing blacked out (timing note only)

description.description: what the model should generate in the black region (no camera words, no quotes)

prompt_spec.description: Structured prompt (H4): structure comes from the input video, these words own the look and additions. No quotes, no camera words.

override.description: gate results the user's pick overrode (policy.explain_generated)

pad_to_seconds.description: Hold the last input frame until this length before sending (models with a minimum output length); the extra output tail is dropped by retime.

role.description: explain: structure-checked hybrid, labels and graphics allowed. mood: generation owns the look, captions only. Default: mood for generative, explain otherwise (studio/generative/policy.py).

scene.description: Declarative scene (studio/layout.py resolves it, blender_ops/layout.py builds it before any author script): data the agent and the user edit instead of code. No expressions, no loops: repetition is repeat/mirror_x, resolved on the host.

use.description: project set merged under this scene (entries replaced by id)

subject.description: a subject spec of this project (subjects/<id>/spec.json), e.g. one written by `subject planetary`

mirror_x.description: also place the mirror image across x = 0

level.description: the fill level this entry stands on (for yields_to_fill)

yields_to_fill.description: left out on its level when the fill brief puts a subject element containing this word there

level_by_z.description: the fill level of each copy along the z repeat (same order as the repeat's z index)

mirror_x.description: also place the mirror image across x = 0

level.description: the fill level this entry stands on (for yields_to_fill)

yields_to_fill.description: left out on its level when the fill brief puts a subject element containing this word there

level_by_z.description: the fill level of each copy along the z repeat (same order as the repeat's z index)

obstacles.description: [x, y, radius] kept clear by fill

mirror_x.description: also place the mirror image across x = 0

backdrop.description: the place around the subject, decided first: a relation (support, view, light) the Blender scene and the backdrop prompt both follow, and the backdrop image once generated (generate backdrop-review --shot) - fixed to the camera, blurred, far behind

distance_m.description: distance from the camera (default: 1.5x the farthest geometry)

margin.description: extra size beyond the subject on each side, in subject sizes (default 3)

behind.description: how far the support reaches behind the subject, away from the view, in subject sizes (default 0.6): the place shows past its edge

elevation_deg.description: how far the camera looks down onto the support; the move and the prompt follow it

azimuth_deg.description: where the camera looks from, as camera moves read azimuth_deg (0 = from -Y); the support reaches toward it

reflections.description: the backdrop image reflected in the subject (a dome only reflections see)

links.description: Objects or collections taken from a .blend file (project-relative path): appended into the scene at `at`; path and hash recorded, so a version never depends on the file
